findings: Keep the correct server flags and PaymentMethod ID versus PaymentIntent ID handoff (source 17–31 and 47–54). The source ends its implementation guidance without the contradictory test row, despite summarizing the `requires_action_not_handled` observation. A maintainer looking up how to interpret a failure in the authentication-required sandbox case could miss the mismatch in a long platform-packed raw.

Source lines 77–82 and the April example at old raw lines 473-508 use `useStripe().handleCardAction`. The 0.84.0 hook exposes the replacement and its implementation accepts the PaymentIntent client secret and optional return URL (`src/hooks/useStripe.tsx:114-122,330-367`, `src/functions.ts:173-201`). Add a version-qualified warning beside the old example and in the reciprocal in-app route (`wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md:115`).

The retained `stripe-ios` snapshot `2026-09-30-7037819` identifies 26.11.0 (`StripePayments.podspec:1-8`). `STPPaymentHandler.swift:2770-2779` deprecates the exact Objective-C selector `handleNextActionForPayment:withAuthenticationContext:returnURL:completion:` from the historical iOS example (old raw lines 99-137 and source lines 58–68) and forwards it to the newer `handleNextActionForPaymentIntent:authenticationContext:returnURL:completion:` path (`STPPaymentHandler.swift:398-411`). The `stripe-android` snapshot `2026-10-27-bb0d8d0` identifies 23.25.1 (`gradle.properties:24-27`). It retains `handleNextActionForPayment` and `onPaymentResult`, with an AndroidX `ComponentActivity` activity overload and a separate fragment overload (`Stripe.kt:280-329,344-368`). Put the warning alongside the historical raw route (source lines 89–91) without changing the April guide's separately documented `confirmation_method` and `use_stripe_sdk` roles.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-mobile-upgrade-to-handle-actions-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-upgrade-to-handle-actions.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/upgrade-to-handle-actions`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobile/upgrade-to-handle-actions states the goal of migrating a basic mobile card integration to handle issuer authentication and routes iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-15). The April 23, 2026 guide assumes the prior no-action card integration and a merchant server endpoint. A client-supplied PaymentMethod ID starts the payment attempt. The server removes `error_on_requires_action` and creates and confirms the card PaymentIntent with `confirmation_method: 'manual'` and `use_stripe_sdk: true` (old raw lines 12-41). The server's `succeeded` branch can trigger fulfillment immediately. On `requires_action`, the server returns the PaymentIntent client secret so the applicable mobile SDK can prompt authentication. Successful action leaves the PaymentIntent in `requires_confirmation`.
